result.markdown: --- title: "Session 3 — Generalised Additive Models (GAM)" subtitle: "Smooth terms · edf · REML · checking k · binary GAMs · smooths by group · Lab 3" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 2: you choose the **knots and df** yourself - Today: a **GAM** lets the **data choose the smoothness** (with a penalty) - By the end you can: - fit a GAM with `mgcv::gam()` and read **edf** - **check** the basis with `gam.check()` - fit a **binary** GAM - let a curve **differ by group** ::: # Topic 1 — The model {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## A GAM for SBP ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} g1 <- gam(sbp ~ s(age) + s(bmi) + s(activity) + salt + sex + smoker, data = ncd, method = "REML") summary(g1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Family: gaussian Link function: identity Formula: sbp ~ s(age) + s(bmi) + s(activity) + salt + sex + smoker Parametric coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 104.0292 0.6972 149.212 < 2e-16 *** salt 0.6506 0.0722 9.012 < 2e-16 *** sexMale 2.7612 0.3719 7.425 1.38e-13 *** smoker 1.3587 0.4181 3.249 0.00117 ** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Approximate significance of smooth terms: edf Ref.df F p-value s(age) 3.899 4.835 202.74 <2e-16 *** s(bmi) 4.076 5.056 64.45 <2e-16 *** s(activity) 3.089 3.900 27.07 <2e-16 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 R-sq.(adj) = 0.311 Deviance explained = 31.4% -REML = 15346 Scale est. = 125.21 n = 4000 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - `s(x)`: a **penalised smooth**; `salt`, `sex`, `smoker` stay **linear** - **method = "REML"**: chooses the **amount of smoothing** from the data - **edf** = effective degrees of freedom: **1 = straight line**, larger = more curved. Age **3.9**, BMI **4.1**, activity **3.1** - The parametric part reads like a normal regression (salt +0.65 mmHg per g/day) ::: ## The curves ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} par(mfrow = c(1, 3)); plot(g1, shade = TRUE, ylab = "Effect on SBP (mmHg)") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s3_gam_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.key} Each panel is the **partial effect** of one variable (others held fixed), with a **95% band**. Age **bends at about 45**, BMI **flattens** (diminishing returns), activity **flattens** too. ::: ## Is it better than a straight line? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} AIC(m_l <- lm(sbp ~ age + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, data = ncd), g1) |> round(0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` df m_l <- lm(sbp ~ age + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, data = ncd) 8 g1 18 AIC m_l <- lm(sbp ~ age + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, data = ncd) 30771 g1 30692 ``` ::: ::: The GAM has **AIC 30,692** against **30,771** for the straight-line model: clearly better. # Topic 2 — Checking {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Is k big enough? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} gam.check(g1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Method: REML Optimizer: outer newton full convergence after 5 iterations. Gradient range [-0.008028857,2.741888e-05] (score 15345.67 & scale 125.212). Hessian positive definite, eigenvalue range [0.927303,1996.511]. Model rank = 31 / 31 Basis dimension (k) checking results. Low p-value (k-index<1) may indicate that k is too low, especially if edf is close to k'. k' edf k-index p-value s(age) 9.00 3.90 1.00 0.42 s(bmi) 9.00 4.08 1.00 0.41 s(activity) 9.00 3.09 0.99 0.40 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - `k` is the **maximum** flexibility (default 10); `edf` should be **well below k'** - The **k-index** is about **1** with **p ≈ 0.4**: k is **adequate** - A **low k-index with a small p and edf close to k'**: refit with a **larger `k`**, e.g. `s(age, k = 15)` - Also look at the **residual plots** (normality, constant variance) ::: # Topic 3 — Binary outcomes and groups {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## A logistic GAM ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g2 <- gam(cvd10 ~ s(age) + s(bmi) + sex + smoker, data = ncd, family = binomial, method = "REML") round(summary(g2)$s.table, 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` edf Ref.df Chi.sq p-value s(age) 1.00 1.00 263.58 0 s(bmi) 4.97 6.07 230.95 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(g2, select = 2, trans = plogis, shift = coef(g2)[1], seWithMean = TRUE, xlab = "BMI", ylab = "10-year CVD risk") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s3_gam_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.key} The BMI smooth has **edf 5.0**: very curved (**U-shaped**); the age smooth has **edf 1.0**: a **straight line on the logit scale**. The GAM **discovered both** without being told. ::: ## A curve for each group ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g3 <- gam(sbp ~ s(age, by = sex) + sex + s(bmi) + s(activity) + salt + smoker, data = ncd, method = "REML") round(AIC(g1, g3), 0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` df AIC g1 18 30692 g3 21 30686 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - `s(age, by = sex)`: **a separate age curve for men and for women** - AIC **30,686 vs 30,692**: a tiny gain, so the curves are **alike**: keep the simpler model - Keep **`sex` as a main effect** too when you use `by = sex` ::: ## GAM or natural spline? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} nd <- data.frame(age = c(30, 45, 70), bmi = mean(ncd$bmi), salt = mean(ncd$salt), activity = mean(ncd$activity), sex = factor("Male", levels = levels(ncd$sex)), smoker = 0) m_ns <- lm(sbp ~ ns(age, df = 4) + bmi + salt + activity + sex + smoker, data = ncd) round(cbind(gam = predict(g1, nd), ns = predict(m_ns, nd)), 1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` gam ns 1 107.7 107.8 2 112.5 112.2 3 126.0 125.7 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **Practically identical** (107.7 vs 107.8; 112.5 vs 112.2; 126.0 vs 125.7). The GAM **chooses the df for you**; a spline with a few df is **easier to explain and to refit** in other software. Both are fine; **report the plot**. ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 3 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `curves-workshop/labs/lab3_gam.R` - GAM for SBP, smooth plots, AIC - `gam.check`, a logistic GAM - smooth by sex, GAM vs natural spline ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k3q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ts5drs.nhu7q" data-show="VGhlIGN1cnZlIGlzIGVzc2VudGlhbGx5IGEgc3RyYWlnaHQgbGluZQ==" data-explain="VGhlIGVmZmVjdGl2ZSBkZWdyZWVzIG9mIGZyZWVkb20gbWVhc3VyZSB0aGUgY3VydmF0dXJl LiBBbiBlZGYgb2YgMSBpcyB0aGUgc2FtZSBhcyBhIHN0cmFpZ2h0IGxpbmUu"} In a GAM summary a smooth term has an edf of 1.0. What does that mean? - The curve is essentially a straight line - The smooth has a single knot at the median - The variable explains one percent of the variance - The smooth has failed and the model must be refitted ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k3q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ts5r0i.ni8p4" data-show="SXQgY2hvb3NlcyB0aGUgYW1vdW50IG9mIHNtb290aGluZyBmcm9tIHRoZSBkYXRh" data-explain="UkVNTCBlc3RpbWF0ZXMgdGhlIHNtb290aGluZyBwZW5hbHR5LCBzbyB0aGUgZGF0YSBkZWNp ZGUgaG93IHdpZ2dseSBlYWNoIGN1cnZlIGlzLCBpbnN0ZWFkIG9mIHRoZSBhbmFseXN0IGNo b29zaW5nIHRoZSBkZi4="} What does method = "REML" do in gam()? - It removes the random effects from the model before fitting - It chooses the amount of smoothing from the data - It refits the model using only the residuals from the first fit - It rounds the smooth terms to whole degrees of freedom ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k3q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ts6499.nin6j" data-show="UmVmaXQgd2l0aCBhIGxhcmdlciBrLCBiZWNhdXNlIHRoZSBiYXNpcyBpcyB0b28gc21hbGwg Zm9yIHRoZSBjdXJ2ZQ==" data-explain="V2hlbiB0aGUgZWRmIGFwcHJvYWNoZXMgaycgdGhlIGJhc2lzIHJlc3RyaWN0cyB0aGUgY3Vy dmUuIEEgbGFyZ2VyIGsgYWxsb3dzIHRoZSBzbW9vdGggdG8gY2FwdHVyZSB0aGUgc2hhcGUs IGFuZCB0aGUgcGVuYWx0eSBzdGlsbCBwcmV2ZW50cyBvdmVyZml0dGluZy4="} gam.check shows a low k-index with a small p-value, and the edf is close to k'. What should you do? - Reduce k, because the curve already has too many degrees of freedom in it - Replace the smooth by a straight line in the model and refit the data - Ignore it, because k only affects the plot and does not affect the fit - Refit with a larger k, because the basis is too small for the curve ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k3q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ts6hhv.nj1nt" data-show="QSBzcGxpbmUgd2l0aCBhIGZldyBkZiBpcyBvZnRlbiBlbm91Z2g7IHRoZSBHQU0gcGlja3Mg aXRzIG93biBkZg==" data-explain="Qm90aCBhcmUgZmxleGlibGUgc21vb3RoIGN1cnZlcy4gV2hlbiB0aGUgc2hhcGUgaXMgc2lt cGxlLCBhIGZldyBkZiBhcmUgZW5vdWdoIGFuZCB0aGUgdHdvIGFwcHJvYWNoZXMgYWdyZWUu "} The GAM and a natural spline with 4 df give almost the same predictions. What does this tell you? - A spline with a few df is often enough; the GAM picks its own df - The GAM is wrong, since it should give a curve different from the spline - Both models are overfitted to the same noise in the sample of adults - The data must be linear, since the two curves agree so closely with each other ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="k3q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="ts6uqm.njg58" data-show="QSBzZXBhcmF0ZSBhZ2UgY3VydmUgZm9yIGVhY2ggc2V4" data-explain="VGhlIGJ5IGFyZ3VtZW50IGZpdHMgb25lIHNtb290aCBwZXIgbGV2ZWwgb2YgdGhlIGZhY3Rv ci4gQSBtYWluIGVmZmVjdCBvZiBzZXggYWxvbmUgb25seSBzaGlmdHMgYSBzaW5nbGUgY3Vy dmUgdXAgb3IgZG93bi4="} What does s(age, by = sex) give? - The age smooth multiplied by the sex variable - Age adjusted for sex before the smooth is fitted - A separate age curve for each sex - One age curve, shifted up or down for each sex ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **`gam(y ~ s(x) + ..., method = "REML")`** - **edf** 1 = straight line; higher = more curved - `gam.check`: k-index, edf vs k' - Binary outcome: `family = binomial`; plot with `trans = plogis` - `by =` for group-specific curves; **plots are the result** ::: **Next:** Session 4: interaction and effect modification

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
